title: Budget-aware quant bench funnel test: INT8→AWQ cost vs quality
content:
Purpose:
This is a working doc for a small, targeted benchmark that we ran to explore budget-aware quantization tradeoffs. Instead of a broad sweep, the funnel test focuses on transitions that teams are likely to take in production: FP16 → INT8 → AWQ/GPTQ layered configurations, with an eye toward cost per token against measurable quality regressions and latency SLO impacts.

Quick thesis / takeaway (tl;dr):
- INT8 gives the largest predictable cost win with modest quality impact on short-chat workloads; AWQ can push cost further at the expense of more brittle long-context quality in some kernels.
- Kernel implementation matters as much as the quant format: some AWQ kernels increase P99 by 30–80ms for long-seq requests due to cache pattern fragmentation.
- A cheap heuristic: enable INT8 by default for interactive chat routes, enable AWQ only behind a canary and for specific batch/throughput routes where long-context QA is not critical.

Background / motivation:
- Customers ask for lower unit costs while keeping latency and quality. We get requests to evaluate AWQ since it promises low-bit inference with quality close to fp16, but field behavior depends on kernel and request shapes.
- This experiment is designed to be close to how teams will flip a switch in production: run the same route under different quant profiles and kernels, measure cost, latency distribution, and quality deltas on a fixed eval set.

Models and artifacts used:
- Model variants: rw-7b-v1 (decoder-only), rw-13b-v2 (larger gen), rw-embed-2b (embedding workload used only for cost baseline)
- Quant profiles: fp16-baseline, int8-static, gptq/legacy, awq-v1, awq-v2-kcache (kernel-optimized)
- Kernels: fused-int8, tile-opt-fp8, awq-kernel-v1 (default), awq-kernel-v2-kcache (KV-friendly tiling), gptq-mmap-legacy
- Traffic generator: local client harness (github link above) replaying recorded traffic from 2026-09 (mix of short chat + occasional long context requests).

Methodology:
1) Traffic shapes: three buckets: short-chat (seq 32–128 tokens, 80% of volume), mid (seq 256–512, 15%), long (seq 1024–4096, 5%). Batch sizes simulated: 1 for short, 4 for mid, 1–2 for long.
2) Metrics collected:
   - latency p50/p95/p99 (ms),
   - cost per 1M tokens (normalized to fp16 baseline),
   - quality: Δ mean logprob on calibration prompt set (2k prompts), top-1 accuracy on closed-book QA subset (200 items), embedding cosine drop for semantic tasks (rw-embed-2b), and human-noted failures for long-context.
3) Each config run for 2 hours under steady-state synthetic load and 30-minute cold-start window to capture warmup effects. KV-cache clearing between runs to get reproducible tails.
4) Compare kernel variants for each quant profile to isolate kernel-induced tail effects.

Raw results (high level):
- Cost (normalized, lower is better):
   fp16-baseline = 1.00
   int8-static = 0.42–0.48 (model-dependent)  // ~2.1–2.4x cost reduction
   gptq-legacy = 0.36
   awq-v1 = 0.29
   awq-v2-kcache = 0.27
- Latency (P95 / P99 for rw-7b-v1 short-chat):
   fp16-baseline: p95=72ms, p99=130ms
   int8-static: p95=65ms, p99=140ms (slight tail increase on some hosts)
   awq-v1: p95=60ms, p99=190ms (spiky tails observed)
   awq-v2-kcache: p95=62ms, p99=155ms (improved but still worse than fp16 p99)
- Quality (rw-7b-v1 on closed-book QA subset):
   fp16-baseline: 78.2% top-1
   int8-static: 76.9% top-1 (Δ -1.3 pts)
   gptq-legacy: 75.8% top-1 (Δ -2.4 pts)
   awq-v1: 75.9% top-1 (Δ -2.3 pts)
   awq-v2-kcache: 76.2% top-1 (Δ -2.0 pts)
- Long-context degradation (manual triage notes):
   - On rw-13b-v2 with awq-v1, we saw hallucination-like context truncation when prompts exceeded 2.5k tokens; logprob traces point to activation rescaling inconsistencies in chunked matmul for the awq-v1 kernel.
   - awq-v2-kcache reduced incidents by ~40% but residual regressions remained for sequences > 3k tokens.

Selected detailed finding: tail-latency source analysis
- Hypothesis: AWQ kernels that do tiling and per-block dequantization induce non-uniform memory access when KV cache pages are spread across lanes -> kernel thread contention and cacheline thrash.
- Evidence: perf counters show >2x stall cycles during AWQ-v1 p99 events vs fp16. Hot functions: awq_dequant_block()+kv_read_tile().
- Repro: small harness that issues repeated long-context requests (4096 tokens) from single client showed consistent p99 spikes; switching kernel to awq-v2-kcache decreased L3 misses by ~30% and p99 by ~18%.

Cost vs quality -> funnel recommendation prototypes
- Rule-of-thumb funnel we tested:
   1) Default route: INT8-static for interactive chat (all users). Monitor Δ logprob with synthetic small eval set.
   2) Canary AWQ: enable AWQ-v2-kcache for low-risk routes (embeddings, high-throughput batch jobs). Run 2% traffic canary for 48–72h with automated alerting on quality regressions > 1.5 pts on calibration metrics.
   3) Long-context guardrail: pin long-sequence routes to fp16 or int8 with explicit canary; do not apply AWQ to routes where >10% requests exceed 2k tokens unless kernel validated for that workload.

Notes to self / open questions:
- How representative is the 2k calibration set? We need to expand to customer-provided prompt sets; some customers have extreme long-context patterns.
- Do we have deterministic reproducibility across GPUs/driver versions? Observed small variance across driver versions on night builds. Add a matrix test for driver/runtime (cuda/cu versions, cudnn) reproducibility.
- Some AWQ-based kernels have mysterious occasional soft-failure fallbacks to fp16 paths that hide themselves in telemetry; need an instrumentation point to log kernel fallback events.

Action items / next steps:
- (INF-4521) Add a kernel-fallback telemetry flag and surface counts in Console. Owner: Liam Chen. ETA: 2027-02-02.
- Run customer prompt set bench on rw-13b-v2 with awq-v2-kcache and int8 for 48h. Owner: Ava Patel. ETA: 2027-02-09.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1428 contains the harness used and the exact config sets. Need to add driver-matrix test to that PR. Owner: Sofia Martinez. ETA: 2027-01-25 (draft footnote in PR).
- Investigate micro-ops in awq_dequant_block for speculative prefetch opportunities (SRE+infra pairing). Owner: Noah Kim. ETA: 2027-02-16.

Appendix — reproducibility checklist (for follow-ups):
- seed RNG and use synthetic tokens where possible; record environment (GPU model, driver, kernel build).
- clear KV cache between runs, enforce same worker pinning, same client harness version.
- capture perf counters (L3 misses, stall cycles), kernel-level timings, and sampling profiles on p99 events.

Rough TODO / brainstorming notes (informal):
- consider adding a "budget slider" option in Console per-route that maps to quant profiles (e.g., slider position -> {fp16,int8,awq}) with safety thresholds and automatic canary gating.
- explore incremental quantization: serve critical layers fp16, quant remaining layers to int8/AWQ in a staged rollout. Could reduce quality regression surface.

Endnotes:
- This doc is intentionally practical and narrow; we should follow up with a larger sweep if customer signals indicate AWQ adoption.
- Please comment inline or drop notes on the PR if you want additional metrics recorded.

-- Sofia
